title: My Bicycle
source_note: NCERT structural alignment only. Zidd uses original teaching passages, checks, and feedback instead of copying the textbook body.

levels.title: Meet the bicycle parts
levels.focus: use bicycle-part words for their jobs
levels.teaching_goal: Name common bicycle parts and connect each part with what it helps a rider do.

guided_check.teaching_block: A bicycle part has a name and a job. Worked example: a basket carries small things. Do not choose a part only because it is mentioned; match the job.
guided_check.passage: Niko squeezes a lever. The bicycle slows before the gate.
guided_check.prompt: Which part did Niko use to slow down?

bridge.teaching_block: Think about the rider’s body. The part under the rider is the seat; the wheels stay below it. This clue separates two parts that may both look round in a picture.
bridge.passage: Asha sits comfortably while her feet reach the pedals.
bridge.prompt: Which part is directly under Asha?

masterclass.teaching_block: Use the sound as evidence. A bell warns people; a brake changes speed. If you confuse them, ask whether the clue is about hearing or stopping.
masterclass.passage: Before passing two walkers, Veer makes a clear ring-ring sound.
masterclass.prompt: Name the bicycle part that makes the warning sound.

independent_check.teaching_block: Recall the part-and-job links you have practised. Give only the part named by the clue.
independent_check.passage: The front wheel turns when Salma moves one part left or right.
independent_check.prompt: What part does Salma move with her hands?

transfer_check.teaching_block: The same part words help when a bicycle is parked for care, not being ridden. Use the clue about where air goes.
transfer_check.passage: At the repair stand, a mechanic pumps air into the round rubber part.
transfer_check.prompt: Which bicycle part receives the air?

levels.title: Read a safe ride
levels.focus: find an important safety detail in a short passage
levels.teaching_goal: Read two connected sentences and identify the action that keeps the rider safe.

guided_check.teaching_block: Read for the action that protects the head. Worked example: knee pads protect knees. A colour detail may be interesting, but it is not the safety action.
guided_check.passage: Rima chooses a yellow bicycle. Before moving, she fastens her helmet strap.
guided_check.prompt: What does Rima fasten before she rides?

bridge.teaching_block: Find the place word and the movement word together. A safe path matters more than the flowers beside it.
bridge.passage: Kabir stays inside the marked cycle lane. Bright flowers grow beside the lane.

masterclass.teaching_block: When a passage has two actions, ask which one happens before the crossing. Looking both ways is the safety detail.
masterclass.passage: Tanu stops at the crossing and looks left and right. Then she walks her bicycle across.
masterclass.prompt: What does Tanu do before crossing?
accepted_answers: stop and look left and right

independent_check.teaching_block: Now locate the safety detail without answer choices. Keep your response short and tied to the passage.
independent_check.passage: A dog runs near Omar’s path. Omar slows down and gives the dog space.
accepted_answers: slows down and gives the dog space
he slows down and gives the dog space

transfer_check.teaching_block: Apply safe-reading clues to a different wheeled ride. The vehicle changes, but protecting the head remains important.
transfer_check.passage: Megha uses a kick scooter in the courtyard. She puts on protective headgear first.
transfer_check.prompt: What safety item does Megha put on?

levels.title: Words on the move
levels.focus: tell bicycle naming, action, and describing words apart
levels.teaching_goal: Identify whether a chapter word names something, shows an action, or describes it.

guided_check.teaching_block: Action words show what someone or something does. Worked example: in “Birds flap,” flap is the action. Test a word by asking, “Can someone do it?”
guided_check.passage: Mohan pedals up the gentle slope.

bridge.teaching_block: A naming word names a person, place, animal, or thing. The word “shiny” tells how something looks, so it is not the naming word.
bridge.passage: The shiny bell hangs near the handle.
bridge.prompt: Which word names the object that rings?

masterclass.teaching_block: A describing word adds a quality. Remove each choice in turn: without “red” we still have a seat, but we lose its colour.
masterclass.passage: Pia wipes the red seat with a cloth.

independent_check.teaching_block: Use the “can someone do it?” test without choices.
independent_check.passage: The children wheel their bicycles into the shed.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer the word-job test from riding to bicycle care. Look for the word that tells what the cloth is like.
transfer_check.passage: Dad uses a soft cloth to clean the frame.

levels.title: Put safety steps in order
levels.focus: arrange words into clear bicycle-safety sentences
levels.teaching_goal: Build a sentence with who first, the action next, and the remaining detail in a sensible place.

guided_check.teaching_block: A clear sentence often starts with who, then says what happened. Worked example: “checks / Ana / the gate” becomes “Ana checks the gate.”
guided_check.prompt: Which sentence is in the correct order?

bridge.teaching_block: Find the person first, then the action. Keep “the bell” together because those words name one thing.
bridge.prompt: Put the words in the best order.

masterclass.teaching_block: Longer sentences still need the same spine: who + action + detail. Time words such as “before riding” usually come after the main action.
masterclass.passage: Words: before riding / checks / Mira / the brakes
options: Mira checks the brakes before riding.
Before checks Mira riding the brakes.
The brakes before Mira riding checks.
accepted_answers: Mira checks the brakes before riding.
mira checks the brakes before riding

independent_check.teaching_block: Arrange the words without choices. Include every word once.
independent_check.passage: Words: slowly / Arun / near the gate / pedals
independent_check.prompt: Arrange all four parts into one clear riding sentence.
accepted_answers: Arun pedals slowly near the gate.
arun pedals slowly near the gate
Arun pedals near the gate slowly.
arun pedals near the gate slowly

transfer_check.teaching_block: Use sentence order for a maintenance action instead of a riding action.
transfer_check.passage: Words: the loose chain / an adult / fixes
transfer_check.prompt: Arrange the three parts into one clear repair sentence.
accepted_answers: An adult fixes the loose chain.
an adult fixes the loose chain

levels.title: Give a clear safety reminder
levels.teaching_goal: Write a short reminder that names the rider or action and states one useful bicycle-safety idea.

guided_check.teaching_block: A complete reminder says what to do, not just one safety word. Worked example: “Wear shoes on the playground.” has an action and a useful detail.
guided_check.passage: A child is about to ride a bicycle.
guided_check.prompt: Which choice is a complete safety reminder?

bridge.teaching_block: A fragment can sound important but still miss an action. Choose the sentence that tells the rider exactly what to do.
bridge.passage: The cycle lane meets a small road.
bridge.prompt: Which reminder is complete and useful?

masterclass.teaching_block: A strong reminder matches the problem. If the tyre is soft, “Ring the bell” is a full sentence but does not solve the problem.
masterclass.passage: One tyre has very little air.
masterclass.prompt: Which sentence gives the right advice?
options: Ask an adult to fill the tyre.
accepted_answers: Ask an adult to fill the tyre.
ask an adult to fill the tyre

independent_check.teaching_block: Plan your own sentence. Name the safety action and the time or reason it matters. Different correct wordings are welcome.
independent_check.passage: Naveen reaches a busy corner while riding.
independent_check.prompt: Write one complete sentence telling Naveen what to do safely.

concept_slots.description: A safe action at the corner.
Connects the action to the corner or traffic.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Use the same reminder skill away from the road. Think about safe storage so nobody trips.
transfer_check.passage: After playtime, a bicycle is lying across the doorway.
transfer_check.prompt: Write one complete sentence telling what should happen next.

concept_slots.description: Moves or parks the bicycle safely.
Names a place away from the doorway.

items.passage: Lina pushes with her feet on two matching parts. The wheels begin to turn.
A small bag rests on the metal shelf behind the seat.
The rider holds one part with both hands to steer.
A round part touches the road and rolls.
Sahil clips his helmet and checks the gate is open. Then he starts riding.
Nora sees gravel ahead. She slows and keeps both hands on the handlebar.
items.prompt: What does Nora do when she sees gravel?

items.passage: At dusk, Imran wears a bright band so drivers can notice him.
Maya hears a truck near the narrow road. She waits with her bicycle on the side.
accepted_answers: on the side of the road

items.passage: The silver chain turns as Rafi pedals.
A tiny bell rings twice.
The mechanic tightens the bolt.
Zoya parks beside the rack.
Words: checks / the tyre / Ali
Words: a helmet / wears / Sita
Words: near the school / rides / Hamid / carefully
options: Hamid rides carefully near the school.
Carefully the school Hamid near rides.
accepted_answers: Hamid rides carefully near the school.
hamid rides carefully near the school

items.passage: Words: the bicycle / locks / Reena
A rider is leaving with an unfastened helmet strap.
items.prompt: Which is the best complete reminder?

items.passage: Children are walking across the cycle lane.
items.prompt: Which sentence gives a useful reminder to the rider?
options: Slow down and let them cross.
accepted_answers: Slow down and let them cross.
slow down and let them cross

items.passage: Rain has made the path slippery.
options: Ride slowly on the wet path.
accepted_answers: Ride slowly on the wet path.
ride slowly on the wet path

items.passage: Kunal wants to ride, but the brake lever feels loose.
items.prompt: Write one complete sentence giving Kunal safe advice.
